root_cause.text: A race in the CAN ISO-TP socket lifecycle let isotp_release() free the dynamically extended so->tx.buf based only on an interruptible wait for tx.state becoming ISOTP_IDLE, while isotp_sendmsg() still accessed that buffer because tx.state/cmpxchg serialization did not guarantee buffer lifetime.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit explicitly says a signal can interrupt wait_event_interruptible() in close() while tx.state is ISOTP_SENDING, causing isotp_release() to continue and kfree(so->tx.buf) “while sendmsg may still be reading so->tx.buf,” and the patch fixes this by removing the kfree() from isotp_release() and deferring it to sk_destruct in isotp_sock_destruct().

agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE/commit explicitly says a signal can interrupt wait_event_interruptible() in close() while tx.state is ISOTP_SENDING, causing isotp_release() to continue and kfree(so->tx.buf) “while sendmsg may still be reading so->tx.buf,” and the patch fixes this by removing the kfree() from isotp_release() and deferring it to sk_destruct in isotp_sock_destruct().

intent_record.intent_summary: Stop freeing ISO-TP RX and TX buffers in isotp_release() to avoid incorrect teardown-time deallocation.
intent_record.what: Two conditional kfree() blocks in isotp_release() were removed: the check and free of so->rx.buf when it differs from so->rx.sbuf, and the check and free of so->tx.buf when it differs from so->tx.sbuf.
intent_record.how: At runtime, socket release no longer frees dynamically allocated RX and TX buffers in this function, leaving buffer cleanup to some other path or avoiding freeing memory here; this changes teardown behavior by preventing these deallocations during isotp_release().

intent_record.intent_summary: Add an ISO-TP socket destructor that performs standard CAN cleanup and frees dynamically allocated RX/TX extended PDU buffers on socket destruction.
intent_record.what: A new static socket destructor function, isotp_sock_destruct(struct sock *sk), was added. It retrieves the ISO-TP socket structure, calls can_sock_destruct(sk), and conditionally frees so->rx.buf and so->tx.buf when they differ from the embedded small-buffer fields so->rx.sbuf and so->tx.sbuf.
intent_record.how: At socket teardown, this adds cleanup for dynamically allocated extended RX and TX PDU buffers while preserving the existing CAN socket destruction path. It prevents allocated ISO-TP buffers from being left unreleased and avoids freeing the inline static buffers by checking pointer identity first.

intent_record.intent_summary: Restore the ISO-TP socket destructor in isotp_init so socket teardown uses the correct cleanup handler.
intent_record.what: In isotp_init(struct sock *sk), three lines were added before the return: a comment stating the default can_sock_destruct() reference is being reassigned, and an assignment setting sk->sk_destruct = isotp_sock_destruct.
intent_record.how: This makes the socket use the ISO-TP-specific destructor during socket teardown instead of leaving the destructor pointer unchanged, ensuring the intended cleanup path is restored after initialization.

grouping_result.intent: Restore the ISO-TP socket destructor in isotp_init so socket teardown uses the correct cleanup handler.

consistency_review.core_intent: Restore and correct ISO-TP socket teardown by moving RX/TX buffer cleanup into a dedicated socket destructor and wiring that destructor back into initialization.

relevance_review.reason: The root cause is premature freeing of the ISO-TP TX buffer in isotp_release() while isotp_sendmsg() may still use it. This group directly addresses that lifetime bug by removing buffer frees from isotp_release(), moving RX/TX buffer cleanup into the socket destructor, and restoring that destructor in initialization so buffers are freed only at final socket destruction.

candidates.rationale: This directly frees the dynamically extended TX buffer during isotp_release(), which is the core lifetime bug: isotp_sendmsg() could still access so->tx.buf after tx.state-based waiting/cmpxchg failed to guarantee exclusive ownership of the buffer.

This condition guards the premature teardown-time free of the dynamic TX buffer. It embodies the vulnerable path where release logic decides buffer lifetime independently of concurrent send-side access.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the teardown-time deallocation of the dynamically extended TX buffer. The root cause is that isotp_release() could free so->tx.buf after only waiting on tx.state, while isotp_sendmsg() could still access that buffer concurrently because tx.state/cmpxchg did not guarantee buffer lifetime.

This guard controls the vulnerable path that frees the dynamic TX buffer during socket release. It reflects the incorrect lifetime decision in isotp_release(), where buffer ownership was inferred independently of concurrent send-side access.

In this commit, `struct tpcon` gains `u8 *buf; unsigned int buflen; ... u8 sbuf[DEFAULT_MAX_PDU_SIZE];`, and `isotp_init()` sets `so->tx.buf = so->tx.sbuf; ... so->tx.buflen = ARRAY_SIZE(so->tx.sbuf);`. In `isotp_sendmsg()`, the transmit path may replace the static buffer with a dynamically allocated one: `if (size > so->tx.buflen && so->tx.buflen < max_pdu_size) { u8 *newbuf = kmalloc(max_pdu_size, GFP_KERNEL); if (newbuf) { so->tx.buf = newbuf; so->tx.buflen = max_pdu_size; } }`. This matches the vulnerable construct from the root cause: buffer lifetime is now separate from `tx.state` serialization, and teardown frees `so->tx.buf` based only on release-time state/lifecycle assumptions. The shown code does not contain any added synchronization or reference/lifetime protection around `so->tx.buf` in `isotp_release()` versus concurrent `isotp_sendmsg()` access. There is no fix here such as a stronger shutdown synchronization, non-interruptible wait guaranteeing send completion, or deferring/freeing the tx buffer only after all users are excluded. Therefore this commit version contains the bug and does not yet contain the fix.
